name: St. George Terroir Gin
production: Douglas fir and sage distilled separately to limit seasonal variation
Fresh bay laurel and juniper vapor-infused
Other botanicals incl. wok-roasted coriander go in the still pot
Douglas fir from a Mendocino forest, harvested seasonally for fire abatement
history: 1982 | St. George Spirits distillery begins operating
2011 | Terroir Gin released (per Imbibe quote on official page)
expressions: St. George Botanivore Gin | sibling gin
St. George Dry Rye Gin | sibling gin
St. George Dry Rye Reposado Gin | barrel-rested sibling
St. George Valley Gin | sibling gin
serve_official: On the rocks, Martini (2 oz gin, 1 oz dry vermouth, 2 dashes orange bitters, sage leaf), or Collins garnished with fennel and bay leaf
notes: Producer calls it 'a forest in your glass'. GQ: 'One of the most distinctive gins made in America.' Also sold in 200 ml. Backlog year 2007 does not match official 2011 release.
